sections.h2: What should a seller know about the Kalamazoo housing market?
sections.html:
Kalamazoo is the largest of the four Michigan cities covered in this group, and it is also the most renter-heavy. The Census Bureau estimates 72,683 residents as of July 1, 2025, and only 42.3 percent of occupied homes are owner-occupied. A seller here is often dealing with a house near a campus, a house previously rented out, or a long-held family home, and the right sale route depends on which of those describes yours.

You can list with an agent, sell it yourself, or take an as-is offer from a cash buyer. In each case the same city offices, the assessor, the treasurer and the rental inspection team, decide what has to be finished before the deed is recorded with the Kalamazoo County Register of Deeds, whose land records go back to 1831.

sections.h2: How did Kalamazoo grow, and where do homes sit in the city?
sections.html:
Titus Bronson settled the site in 1829 and the town carried his name until 1836, when it took the name of the river. The city covers 25.11 square miles along a bend in the Kalamazoo River, with the flat northeastern part in the river valley and low hills rising to the west and south. Wikipedia counts 22 neighborhoods, many with a neighborhood association that works with the city's Neighborhood Development Division.

I-94 puts Kalamazoo about halfway between Detroit and Chicago, and the city is 50 miles south of Grand Rapids. US 131, M-96 and M-343 connect it to the rest of the region. Amtrak's Wolverine uses a downtown station that is the hub of the only high-speed corridor outside the Northeast, with 110 mile-an-hour service between Porter, Indiana and Albion, Michigan. The Kalamazoo/Battle Creek International Airport sits on the southern edge. A major tornado tore through downtown in 1980, and summers can be hot and humid, while lake-effect snow is common in winter.

sections.h2: What do Census figures show about Kalamazoo households?
sections.html:
The 2020 to 2024 data describe a university city with higher education and mid-range home values:

  • Median value of owner-occupied homes: $179,000.
  • Households: 29,523, with 2.25 persons each.
  • Median gross rent: $1,078.
  • Bachelor's degree or higher among adults 25 and older: 38.5 percent.
  • Living in the same house one year earlier: 75.9 percent, the lowest of the four cities in this group, which fits a city with many students and renters.

Between 2020 and 2025 the estimated population slipped 1.2 percent, so the market is stable rather than surging. A house priced near the $179,000 median that needs work will compete with similar listings, and a buyer who plans to rent it must register it with the city.

sections.h2: Do my schools and the Kalamazoo Promise affect the sale?
sections.html:
Most of the city is served by Kalamazoo Public Schools, with small sections in Parchment, Comstock and Portage districts. Every resident graduate of Kalamazoo Public Schools has been eligible, since the class of 2006, for a scholarship covering up to 100 percent of tuition and mandatory fees for four years at any public university or community college in Michigan. The program is known as the Kalamazoo Promise, and buyers with children often ask about it.

The city is also home to Western Michigan University, Kalamazoo College (founded 1833), Kalamazoo Valley Community College and Davenport University, plus the WMU Homer Stryker School of Medicine, which opened in 2014. Houses near those campuses are more likely to have a rental history, which brings the city's rental rules into play.

sections.h2: How does Kalamazoo's rental certification affect selling a rental?
sections.html:
Every rental property in Kalamazoo must be registered and certified. An inspector issues a Certificate of Compliance after a satisfactory inspection against the Housing Code in Chapter 17 of the city code. The city may inspect each rental at least once every 28 months, and it mails a courtesy notice four months before a certificate expires. Owners are told to schedule the inspection three months out and to book a reinspection within 10 days when violations are found.

Kalamazoo Certificate of Compliance lengths and conditions
CertificateWho qualifies
28 monthsStandard certificate for any rental, and the fallback when a property misses a longer one
40 monthsRenewals issued before the old certificate expires, with no appearance tickets or enforcement letters and no more than six documented violations in the prior cycle
52 monthsRenewals after two straight 40-month certificates, with no conditions and no more than four trash or nuisance violations

Source: City of Kalamazoo Rental Registration Rules and Responsibilities. Give a buyer the certificate's expiration date and any open violations, and ask the rental inspections team to update the owner on the registration form after the sale.

sections.h2: When are Kalamazoo property taxes due, and who gets relief?
sections.html:
Summer bills go out by July 1 and are due by July 31. They can be paid at once or in six monthly payments; if the first installment is missed, the city adds a one-time 3 percent penalty and 1 percent interest on the first of each month. Winter bills are mailed by December 1, due by February 14, and must be paid in full. Anything still unpaid on March 1 becomes delinquent and is paid to the Kalamazoo County Treasurer.

Eligible owners can defer a summer bill to the winter due date if household income was no more than $40,000 the year before and they are 62 or older, disabled, blind, or an eligible veteran, service member or widow or widower. Applications go to the City Treasurer by September 15. Homeowners who live in the house can also claim the principal residence exemption, which the city says cuts an annual bill by more than 25 percent.

sections.h2: What exemption paperwork changes when I sell in Kalamazoo?
sections.html: A seller files a Request to Rescind Principal Residence Exemption with the assessor. A buyer who will live in the house files a new exemption affidavit with the assessor. State law lets an owner who buys a second home keep the exemption on the first home for up to 3 years if the first home is unoccupied, for sale, not leased and not used for business, and the city's FAQ says the owner must re-file the conditional form each year by December 31. Ask the City Assessor's office whether you are using this option before you list.

sections.h2: What does transfer tax come to on a Kalamazoo sale?
sections.html: Use the city's median value as a worked example. A $179,000 sale is 358 units of $500. At the state rate of $3.75 per unit (MCL 207.525) plus the county's 55 cents per unit in a county under 2,000,000 people (MCL 207.504), the seller owes $4.30 times 358, or $1,539.40, to the county treasurer within 15 days of delivering the deed. Family transfers to a child or grandchild, court orders without a stated price and deeds that only confirm existing title are exempt under MCL 207.526.

faqs.q: How often does Kalamazoo inspect a rental?
faqs.a: At least once every 28 months. Properties that renew on time and stay clean can earn 40 or 52 month certificates, so inspections become less frequent.

faqs.q: When are Kalamazoo winter taxes due?
faqs.a: February 14. The bill is mailed by December 1 and must be paid in full. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on March 1 and go to the Kalamazoo County Treasurer.

faqs.q: Can I defer my Kalamazoo summer tax bill?
faqs.a: Yes, if household income last year was no more than $40,000 and you fit a listed group such as age 62 or older or disabled. Apply to the City Treasurer by September 15; the bill is then due with the winter bill.

faqs.q: How much transfer tax applies to a $179,000 Kalamazoo sale?
faqs.a: $1,539.40 in a county under 2,000,000 residents. That is 358 units of $500 at $3.75 state plus $0.55 county, paid by the seller.
